findings.statement: I could not find any public price page or institutional index that published a BTC‑USD spot quote with an explicit per‑second 'as‑of' timestamp matching 2026-08-15T19:21:19Z. The nearest timestamped public snapshots were: TwelveData / Coinbase Pro feed 'Last update' Aug 15, 6:59 PM UTC showing BTC/USD = $62,989.13, and Yahoo Finance 'As of' 7:01:17 PM UTC showing BTC-USD = $62,988.45.

CoinDesk and CoinMarketCap displayed live BTC prices in their pages at the query time, but the available snapshots did not include an explicit per‑second 'As of' or 'Last updated' timestamp that matches 2026-08-15T19:21:19Z.

Across sampled spot providers near the query time the reported BTC/USD prices were: CoinDesk $64,019.00; CoinMarketCap $63,412.05; Yahoo Finance $62,988.45. The observed max–min spread is $1,030.55 (64,019.00 − 62,988.45 = 1,030.55), which is about 1.62% of the three‑provider average ($63,473.17).

Nearest reliable, timestamped public quotes found for the user’s window: TwelveData / Coinbase Pro feed (Last update Aug 15, 6:59 PM UTC) BTC/USD ≈ $62,989.13; Yahoo Finance (As of 7:01:17 PM UTC) BTC-USD = $62,988.45. Other major aggregators (CoinDesk, CoinMarketCap, CoinGecko) published live values but did not expose a per‑second 'as‑of' time in the accessible snapshots.

CME Group's settlements table (snapshot) listed the AUG 26 futures contract settle at 63,455.00. The CME 'Quotes' table snapshot showed front‑month 'Last' values in the low‑to‑mid $62k range (example Last ≈ 62,885 on a quotes snapshot) and the page carried a 'Last Updated' note (14 Aug 2026 06:38:54 AM CT) explaining the quoted values were recent as of Aug 14 in that snapshot.

CME documented that Bitcoin futures moved to near‑continuous Globex trading in late May 2026 with short scheduled maintenance windows (example: a weekly Saturday pause). The stated maintenance window does not cover 19:21:19 UTC on Saturday Aug 15 (it is outside the Saturday 03:00–05:00 UTC maintenance), so CME Globex crypto futures would generally be available for trading at 2026-08-15T19:21:19Z.

Contemporaneous market research and on‑chain analytics indicate the main near‑term drivers for Bitcoin in mid‑August 2026 were: (1) spot‑ETF flows (large but variable—strong weekly inflows early Aug, some daily outflows around Aug 13–14), (2) on‑chain accumulation and net transfers off exchanges supporting supply tightening, (3) macro news (July CPI and related prints) that were largely priced in and produced muted BTC reactions, and (4) neutral-to‑cautious market sentiment (Fear & Greed index readings in the 'fear' range).

The evidence is not uniform: ETF flow reports differ (strong weekly inflows vs short streak outflows mid‑August), macro prints were largely in line with expectations (muted reaction), and on‑chain metrics point to accumulation. Those mixed signals are consistent with the observed range‑bound spot quotes (~$62.9k–$64.0k) at the query time.

final_answer.answer:
Short answer — price: roughly in the low‑to‑mid $63k band at the query time (range ≈ $62,988–$64,019 across major public pages). No public page I found published a per‑second “as‑of” timestamp for 2026‑08‑15 19:21:19 UTC, so the closest timestamped quotes were about 20 minutes earlier: Coinbase/TwelveData “Last update” Aug 15 18:59 UTC = $62,989.13 and Yahoo Finance “As of” 19:01:17 UTC = $62,988.45. Other major pages showed: CoinDesk $64,019.00 and CoinMarketCap $63,412.05 (max–min spread ≈ $1,030.55, ~1.6% of the average). Reported 24‑hour changes in the sampled snapshots were modest and varied by provider (CoinDesk ~+0.27%; CoinMarketCap ~+0.02%; Yahoo ~+0.15%).

CME futures (institutional reference): the AUG‑26 settlement snapshot listed ~63,455.00 and the CME quotes snapshot showed a front‑month “Last” in the low‑to‑mid $62k (example ~62,885). CME has moved to near‑24/7 Globex trading with a short weekly maintenance window, and 19:21 UTC on Aug 15 falls outside that window so futures would generally be tradable then.

Main factors driving Bitcoin at this moment (mid‑Aug 2026) — why price is range‑bound:
- Spot‑ETF flows: mixed signals — large weekly inflows earlier in August but reported net outflows around Aug 14, producing short‑term flow variability and uncertainty. 
- On‑chain activity: Glassnode on‑chain metrics point to accumulation and reduced exchange supply, which tightens available spot liquidity.
- Macro: recent US CPI and related prints were largely priced in; BTC showed a muted reaction, reducing a strong macro‑driven directional move.
- Sentiment: indicators (Fear & Greed) were in the “fear” range (~28–29), consistent with cautious, range‑bound trading.

Bottom line: available public snapshots cluster in the low‑to‑mid $63k area but differ by up to ~1k across providers; mixed ETF flows, underlying on‑chain accumulation, muted macro news, and cautious sentiment explain the range‑bound price action.
